questions.prompt: Which named process has constant volume?
questions.answer: A constant-volume process is called isochoric.

questions.prompt: Which named process has no heat transfer?
questions.answer:
A process with no heat transfer is called adiabatic:
\[
Q=0
\]

questions.prompt: For an isochoric process with \(Q=450\,\mathrm{J}\), find \(W\) and \(\Delta U\).
questions.answer:
Isochoric means constant volume, so
\[
W=0
\]
Then
\[
\Delta U=Q-W=450-0=450\,\mathrm{J}
\]

questions.prompt: For an isobaric expansion at \(p=2.0\times10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}\) with \(\Delta V=0.010\,\mathrm{m^3}\), find \(W\).
questions.answer:
For an isobaric process,
\[
W=p\Delta V
\]
\[
W=(2.0\times10^5)(0.010)=2.0\times10^3\,\mathrm{J}
\]

questions.prompt: An ideal gas expands isothermally and does \(350\,\mathrm{J}\) of work. Find \(\Delta U\) and \(Q\).
questions.answer:
For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature. Isothermal means \(\Delta T=0\), so
\[
\Delta U=0
\]
Then
\[
0=Q-W
\]
so
\[
Q=W=350\,\mathrm{J}
\]

questions.prompt: A gas undergoes an adiabatic compression with \(W=-280\,\mathrm{J}\). Find \(Q\) and \(\Delta U\).
questions.answer:
Adiabatic means
\[
Q=0
\]
Using
\[
\Delta U=Q-W
\]
\[
\Delta U=0-(-280)=280\,\mathrm{J}
\]

questions.prompt: A process is isobaric with \(Q=900\,\mathrm{J}\) and \(W=250\,\mathrm{J}\). Find \(\Delta U\) and state whether temperature rises for an ideal gas.
questions.answer:
\[
\Delta U=Q-W
\]
\[
\Delta U=900-250=650\,\mathrm{J}
\]
For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature. Since \(\Delta U>0\), the temperature rises.

questions.prompt: A cyclic process rejects \(400\,\mathrm{J}\) of heat overall. Find net work done by the system and interpret its sign.
questions.answer:
Rejecting \(400\,\mathrm{J}\) of heat means
\[
Q_{\mathrm{net}}=-400\,\mathrm{J}
\]
For a cycle,
\[
\Delta U=0
\]
so
\[
W_{\mathrm{net}}=Q_{\mathrm{net}}=-400\,\mathrm{J}
\]
The negative sign means the surroundings do net work on the system.

questions.prompt: An ideal gas goes from state \(A\) to state \(B\) with the same temperature by two processes: isothermal expansion and free expansion into vacuum. Compare \(Q\), \(W\), and \(\Delta U\) for the two processes.
questions.answer:
For both processes, the ideal gas has the same initial and final temperature, so
\[
\Delta U=0
\]
For a quasistatic isothermal expansion,
\[
W>0
\]
and the first law gives
\[
Q=W>0
\]
For free expansion into vacuum, there is no opposing pressure, so
\[
W=0
\]
If the free expansion is isolated,
\[
Q=0
\]
The endpoint temperature can be the same for an ideal gas even though the heat and work transfers are different.

questions.prompt: A gas is heated from \(T_i\) to \(T_f\) once at constant volume and once at constant pressure. For an ideal gas, derive which path requires more heat and by how much per mole.
questions.answer:
At constant volume,
\[
Q_V=nC_V\Delta T
\]
At constant pressure,
\[
Q_P=nC_P\Delta T
\]
For an ideal gas,
\[
C_P-C_V=R
\]
so
\[
Q_P-Q_V=nR\Delta T
\]
Per mole, the constant-pressure path requires extra heat
\[
R\Delta T
\]
because some of the heat input becomes expansion work.
